gen-megrim-gf-menbere: Sharp, wiry, a little sci-fi: Megrim draws every stroke at one measured thickness. And Menbere, a plain sans, stacks its tall lowercase like rolled cord and does the quiet work of carrying text.
gen-megrim-gf-mitr: Megrim's strokes all share one measured width, giving its angular letters a futuristic, drafted look. Mitr sits beside it, friendly and compact.
gen-megrim-gf-momo-trust-display: Megrim draws angular, futuristic letters with no thick or thin variation anywhere in them, each stroke the same. Momo Trust Display follows in generous, drifting sans-serif forms.
gen-megrim-gf-mukta: Angular and spare, almost like wire bent into letters. Megrim earns its keep big and brief, while Mukta, a sans-serif with tall-bodied small letters, handles the rest.
gen-megrim-gf-mukta-mahee: Chunky and tall in the lowercase, Mukta Mahee reads as friendly and approachable. Mukta Mahee against Megrim's hairline-free, futuristic angles is what makes this pair memorable.
gen-megrim-gf-mukta-malar: Megrim's marker-like line never changes weight, which gives it a crisp futuristic edge. It is best for bold, angular statements, while Mukta Malar, a sans with compressed ascenders, is best at quietly carrying approachable text.
gen-megrim-gf-mukta-vaani: Megrim draws its angular, futuristic letters with plain constant-width lines, nothing thick or thin. Mukta Vaani sits below with a high-waisted lowercase.
gen-megrim-gf-narnoor: Round-tipped pen lines, cut into angles. Megrim is built to grab attention, while Narnoor, a plain sans with short ascenders above big bowls, is built to be read.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-display: No hairline appears anywhere in Megrim, which keeps its angular, futuristic letters uniform. Noto Sans Display answers with a big, tall middle zone in every word.
gen-megrim-gf-port-lligat-sans: Megrim has no hairlines to squint at, so its angular futuristic letters hold up even small. Port Lligat Sans, tightly packed sans-serif, is better at reading.
